name: 1712 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12

function.note: The 1911 sheet draws the building crossed by one X, the key's sign for a stable (the T-1840 census: '2-storey brick stable (X) on the alley'), and Robinson's 1886 plate 10 crosses the brick building it draws on the same ground behind lot 3, the atlas's stable. Carried to 1904 between the two, INFERRED; no source names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

research_note: T-1932 refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit. The sheet census (census row s20-1712-r1, trace s20fp-1712-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. The kit stands as drawn, its party wall at the north end, where the building's north wall stands on the lot line, and its open gable to the south, where the sheet marks no window. The sheet's one window mark, on the alley wall at its middle, is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it. Robinson's 1886 plate draws a crossed brick stable of about the same size on the same ground, so it stood from before 1886 through 1911. No picture of it is known. The reading is in docs/RESEARCH/k12-1712-stable-1932/README.md.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 rests on two maps either side of it. Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws a pink, crossed building on the alley behind lot 3 (house number 1712 in its margin), about 8.2 m deep (columns 346.1-369.9) by 12.7 m along the alley (rows 1455.9-1492.5), half-height edges of pink-density profiles on the committed plate raster at its 0.346 m a pixel, which take in the plate's own border lines: within two of its pixels, the building the 1911 sheet draws, 7.64 by 11.99 m. The 1911 sheet draws it again, so it stood from before 1886 through 1911 and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), as the district draft did. FROM: the record claims the 1904 target and no earlier day. TO: the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

position.symbolic_location: 1712 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: on the alley, its north wall on the lot line, parcel prairie_1712 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json): local E 1335.289, N -3118.610. The fit's own residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed; the draft stood the building inside a rectangle fitted to its trace.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is pixel (2224.27, 4516.66) of the committed sheet 20 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 2224.3) to its east wall line (2374.7) and from its north wall line, on the lot line (row 4398.6), to its south wall line (4634.7), each the peak of a median darkness profile: 150.4 by 236.1 pixels at the sheet's 0.050779 m a pixel, 7.639 m deep by 11.986 m along the alley.

stories.note: '2' lettered on the building: two storeys.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with wall thicknesses lettered '12 8' (inches, the first storey's and the second's, as the key reads them) inside its north and south walls. Robinson's 1886 plate also colours it pink, its brick.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the sheet's window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1712-stable-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 8', a stable's X, and one of the key's window marks, on the alley wall about 5.91 m from the north wall line and 6.08 m from the south, with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there). It draws no fire-wall sign and no other mark on this building. The kit stands as drawn: its party wall at the north end, where the building's north wall stands on the lot line; its open gable at the south end, 4.6 m short of 1720's building, with no opening, as the sheet marks none. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley wall's from the north end, the yard wall's from the south end, as the kit lays them). The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s 5.58). The carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch over it toward the north end, and a man door with a loft sash over it toward the south end, are the kit's. The yard wall has a door onto the workyard at its middle between two stable sash and two loft sash. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at the kit's own 40 degrees over the 7.64 m span, about 3.2 m from eave to ridge: the deep stables (1616, 1612, 1626, 1628, 1736) took 30 degrees over 11-15 m, and this one is shallow from the alley. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the sheet's solid dot inside the building about 0.7 m from its south wall and 6.1 m from the alley, the key's sign for a vertical steam boiler (the kit has no stack, and the sheet draws none). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the frame end at the back of the house's rear wing, 17.3 m east of the yard wall.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot with the sheet's window mark where it puts them, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.
